title: What If Hell and Paradise Are Just the End of Denial? - Thursday: Maamar Yafeh Sha'ah Achas #10
blurb: Letting Go: How the Ache of Our Generation Can Open Us to the Bliss of Redemption What if paradise vs. hell is the experience of re-experiencing your life, but this time without denial? The imagery of fire and snow, snakes and scorpions, gives form to something deeply personal. Your own choices and passions come back to you, and this time you feel them from the deepest truth of who you are. You see your preciousness, your capacity to love, and the divine presence within your human life. From that place, you relive the moments you went numb to get through something, the years you spent trying to win approval, and the choices in which you betrayed your soul. The pleasure that once helped you escape can return as pain of equal intensity. You can finally feel what you gave up for that pleasure. And that very pain allows you to purge the filth and move freely into the bliss of oneness. The Mitteler Rebbe takes this a step further. In His grace, Hashem gives us a chance to go through this purging and cleansing in our lifetime. That is the startling meaning in Avraham’s prayer for Gehenom in this world. A person can have everything that looks like success and still feel an ache inside. Sometimes that ache is truth banging on the walls of a life we built to feel secure. We can patch the crack and reach for another layer of control, or we can let it open and see what our defenses have kept us from feeling. title: Coal and Pearls: Discovering Your Light and your Bliss - Likkutei Sichos Yud-Tes Kislev
blurb: The Dual Contribution of Chassidus to Judaism This text-based class, in Likkutei Sichos vol. 20 Yud Yes Kislev, explains the dual function of Chassidus, described both as coal and pearls. Coal is found in the earth; pearls in the sea. Coal are vital for life; pearls are luxury. For one, Chassidus presented a depth and sophisticated to Judaism that would allow it to withstand the onslaught of modernity in all of its manifestations. In addition, Chassidus introduced a new consciousness as a foretaste of the times of Moshiach. View Source Sheets: https://portal.theyeshiva.net/api/source-sheets/2612

title: Samach Vav Part 255: Two ways to serve G-d, and two types of souls: Son and servant
blurb: Samach Vav p. 206: [To understand the power of self-generated effort, which draws down new, unprecedented energy, and the way the light becomes integrated and revealed in existence, a lengthy discussion begins about two types of service and two types of souls: The soul of Atzilut is an extension of the Divine, and therefore serves like a son who has access to the inner revelations of the Divine. The soul of B’iya is a “new” entity outside the Divine and serves like a servant through hard work, earning its right to the divine through exertion (unlike a son who naturally inherits his father’s wealth). Essentially, the underlying theme is to explain how deep we can reach and how much it becomes ours; how new the revelation is and how much it is integrated into our beings; how we reach the essence and we also reveal it in our parameters.] Question: Why is there a need for avodah b'koach atzmo (self-generated effort), (why is self-generated effort ultimately necessary) and what is its contribution when the love and reverence from above is a superior state (of revelation)? (Answer in Maamar 26; 40-42. pp 519. 525. 532). There are two levels -- a son and a servant. At times souls are called sons, and at times servants. Specifically, there are two types of souls: 1. Servant -- soul from nara"n of biy"a, who has a rational understanding of G-d ("knows G-d in a general way"). 2. title: Chapter 37.06: Building a Healthy World
blurb: Chapter 37.06: Building a Healthy World The Tanya Applied radio show is broadcast every Saturday night, 10–10:30PM ET on WSNR 620 AM – Metro NY area WJPR 1640 AM — Highland Park and Edison, NJ Online: www.talklinenetwork.com By phone: Listen Line: 641-741-0389 Many of us may be familiar with some of the central ideas in Tanya – including the battle of the two souls; what defines man and makes us tick; how we can control our temptations; how we can become more loving; what we can do to curb and harness our vices, like anger, jealousy, and depression; the formula for growth; how we can develop a healthy relationship with G-d; and why we are here. In this 30-minute program, you will learn how these ideas can be applied to your life today. You will discover secrets to a successful life that will transform you and your relationships. Rabbi Simon Jacobson is the best-selling author of Toward a Meaningful Life, and he is the creator of the acclaimed and popular MyLife: Chassidus Applied series, which has empowered and transformed hundreds of thousands through Torah and Chassidus. Now, Rabbi Jacobson brings his vast scholarship and years of experience to Tanya. Please join Rabbi Simon Jacobson for this exhilarating journey into your psyche and soul. You will come away with life-changing practical guidance and direction, addressing all the issues and challenges you face in life. title: ‘Is Chabad for Everyone?’ A Debate on Living Chassidus
